record.paper_title: Recent results and open problems on parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearities
record.context_brief: Existence, uniqueness, and universality of critical self-similar blowup
record.original_question: In the whole space R^N, consider the equation u_t - Δu = |u|^{p-1}u - b|∇u|^q in the scaling-invariant case q = 2p/(p+1). Theorem 2.8 constructs positive radial backward self-similar blowup solutions of the form u(t,x) = (T-t)^(-1/(p-1)) W(x/(T-t)^{1/2}) for 0 < b < 2 and for p in a non-explicit interval 1 < p < p_0(b,N). What are the actual admissible values of p for such self-similar blowup, can the existence result be extended to all p > 1 and all b > 0, is the self-similar solution unique for fixed parameters, and is the profile from Theorem 2.8 the universal blowup profile in the critical case q = 2p/(p+1), or can qualitatively different blowup profiles occur?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.8 Assume Ω = R^N, q = 2p/(p+1), and 0 < b < 2. There exists p0 = p0(b, n) > 1, such that for all p with 1 < p < p0, the equation (1.6) has a solution of the form (2.5) with m = 1/2, where W is positive, C^2, radially symmetric and radially decreasing in R^N.

Open problem 3. The value of p0 in Theorem 2.8 is not explicitly known (because the proof involves a limiting argument). Can one specify the allowable values of p, or even extend the result to all p > 1, and also to all b > 0? On the other hand, is the self-similar solution unique for each value of the parameters? Is the self-similar profile of Theorem 2.8 representative of all blowup behaviors when q = 2p/(p + 1), or do there exist different profiles?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the semilinear parabolic equation
  u_t − Δu = |u|^{p−1} u − b |∇u|^q,    (t,x) ∈ (0,T) × R^N,
with N ≥ 1, p > 1, q > 1, and b > 0. Choose the scaling-invariant exponent q = 2p/(p+1), so that the equation is invariant under the rescaling u_λ(t,x) = λ^{2/(p−1)} u(λ^2 t, λ x).

A backward self-similar blowup solution at time T > 0 is a solution of the form
  u(t,x) = (T − t)^{−1/(p−1)} W( x / (T − t)^{1/2} ),
where the profile W : R^N → R satisfies the elliptic equation
  ΔW − (1/2) y · ∇W − W/(p−1) + |W|^{p−1} W − b |∇W|^q = 0,    y ∈ R^N.

It is known that for every N ≥ 1 and every b ∈ (0,2) there exists some p_0 = p_0(b,N) > 1 (defined non-explicitly through a limiting argument) such that for every p ∈ (1, p_0) the profile equation admits a solution W that is positive, of class C^2, radially symmetric, and radially decreasing on R^N.

Answer the following:
(a) Determine the actual set of admissible exponents p > 1 for which such positive, radial, radially decreasing self-similar profiles exist.
(b) Decide whether the existence statement can be extended to all p > 1 and all b > 0.
(c) For each fixed admissible pair (p,b,N), decide whether the positive radial self-similar profile W is unique.
(d) In the critical case q = 2p/(p+1), decide whether every blowup of (positive) solutions of the equation is asymptotically described by such a self-similar profile, or whether qualitatively different blowup behaviors can occur.
artifact.category_tag: self-similar blowup for parabolic equations with gradient nonlinearity
artifact.status_search_result: Web search indicates that existence of positive radial backward self-similar profiles for the critical case q = 2p/(p+1) is established only for 0 < b < 2 and p − 1 sufficiently small via a non-explicit limiting argument. The questions of the precise admissible range of p, extension to all p > 1 and all b > 0, uniqueness of the profile, and universality of the self-similar profile among all blowup behaviors remain active and unresolved problems in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Self-similar blow-up profiles for a reaction-diffusion equation with critical weighted reaction (and related works on gradient-perturbed semilinear heat equations)
status_evidence.snippet: Existence and properties of self-similar profiles in critical regimes are established under restrictions on parameters; uniqueness and universality remain open in many regimes.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of self-similar blowup profiles is known under parameter restrictions while uniqueness/universality is generally open.

status_evidence.title: Self-Similar Blow-Up Solutions of the KPZ-type Equation
status_evidence.snippet: For ∂_t Ψ = ΔΨ − b|∇Ψ|^q + |Ψ|^{p−1}Ψ with 0 < b < 2, q = 2p/(p+1), and p−1 small, a non-trivial backward self-similar solution exists; the precise admissible range and uniqueness are not fully characterized.
status_evidence.claim: Existence holds for small p−1 and b<2; precise range, uniqueness and universality are not established.
